title: Trimming and Normalizing Strings
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of trimming and normalizing strings and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—trim()—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study trimming and normalizing strings with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you process text correctly while accounting for immutability, equality, and Unicode. In this lesson, focus on trim() and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: String values are immutable, so methods return new results rather than changing existing text. Compare contents with `equals`, and distinguish UTF-16 code units from Unicode code points and visible graphemes. Apply that reasoning specifically to trim() and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect trim() with strip(), stripleading(), and striptrailing() before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.
